title: Etale field cover of a reduced locally Noetherian singleton stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal Z$ a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic stack over $S$ such that $|\mathcal Z|$ has exactly one point. Assume the relative diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/S}$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism], meaning that each scheme base change, on etale scheme charts of its algebraic-space source, is unramified. There are a field $k$ [def-weil-field] and a representable-by-algebraic-spaces surjective etale morphism $z:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal Z$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ or perfectness hypothesis on $k$ is imposed. An algebraic stack over $S$ means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre product, and representability use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space], and smooth uses [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Its point set consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism over a common field extension. A stack is reduced and locally Noetherian when it admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas which is reduced and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; reduced means every local ring has no nonzero nilpotents. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts.

source.place: Tag 06N0 (lemma-DM-residual-gerbe); relative-base formulation by Tag 050N (lemma-separated-implies-morphism-separated), (1). DM here means unramified diagonal, not an already constructed etale atlas.

proof.text: Apply the flat-field-cover lemma to obtain a field $K$ and a representable surjective flat locally finitely presented map $a:U=\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal Z$. The given smooth atlas also implies fppf descent for $\mathcal Z$. Form its self-relation $R=U\times_{\mathcal Z}U$ with source, target and composition given by the two projections and composition of the displayed isomorphisms. The fppf presentation lemma gives flat locally finitely presented $s,t:R\to U$ and an equivalence $[U/R]\simeq\mathcal Z$. In particular $s,t$ are locally of finite type by chartwise calculus. No etale atlas is used.

The map $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ is exactly the scheme base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/S}$ by $a\times a$, so it is unramified by the hypothesis. The field-groupoid identity-component lemma applies: $R$ is a separated scheme, $j$ is separated and locally quasi-finite, and the identity component $P=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is open and closed in $R$. Its operations restrict to a groupoid, both projections to $U$ are finite locally free, and $P\to U\times_SU$ is a monomorphism. These are statements about the relative relation over $S$, so no passage to an absolute diagonal or hypothesis on $S$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 06N0, first paragraph: stabilizer dimension, 06FF, 06LZ, 06LH, and the component containing the identity.

proof.text: Apply division by a finite flat subrelation to $(U,R,P)$. Its hypotheses hold by step 2 and affineness of $U$. Obtain $q:U\to\bar U=U/P$, finite locally free and surjective, and a scheme groupoid $(\bar U,\bar R)$ whose restriction along $q$ is $(U,R)$. The affine finite-flat-relation quotient theorem identifies $\bar U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ for the equalizer $k_0=\{b\in K:s^\sharp(b)=t^\sharp(b)\text{ in }B\}$. This identification is compatible with $q$, because both objects represent the same fppf quotient. The equalizer contains $0,1$ and is closed under ring operations. If $b\ne0$ belongs to it, both images are equal units, so their inverses are equal and $b^{-1}$ also belongs to it. Thus $k_0$ is a field. Notice that these are the $P$-invariants, not the invariants of the whole relation $R$.

source.place: Tag 06N0, finite-flat quotient and invariant-field argument; bootstrap.tex 04S4; groupoids.tex 03BM.

proof.text: The map $q$ is an fppf cover. The restriction equivalence gives $[\bar U/\bar R]\simeq[U/R]\simeq\mathcal Z$, compatibly with the maps from $U$. The map $R\to\bar R$ is the base change of $q\times q$ along $(\bar s,\bar t)$, hence is surjective flat locally finitely presented by chartwise base change and composition. To check flatness and local finite presentation of $\bar s$, use the target cover $q:U\to\bar U$ and the source cover $R\to\bar R\times_{\bar U,\bar s}U$; the latter is the base change of the other copy of $q$ in the restriction formula. The resulting composite to $U$ is $s$. The source-and-target locality lemma descends both properties. The same argument with $t$ proves that $\bar t$ is flat and locally finitely presented. This explicitly handles both copies of $q$ rather than identifying $s$ itself with a single target base change of $\bar s$.

source.place: Tag 06N0, second and third paragraphs: 04S4, 046T and descent of the projections.

proof.text: Pull back the unit $\bar e:\bar U\to\bar R$ by the fppf cover $R\to\bar R$. The unit clause of the division lemma identifies its preimage $R\times_{\bar R,\bar e}\bar U$ with $P$, and the resulting map to $R$ is the original inclusion of the subrelation: arrows above an identity are precisely the arrows of $P$, which is $U\times_{\bar U}U$. This identification respects both projections by the kernel-pair conclusion of step 3. The inclusion $P\to R$ is open, so target-local descent for open immersions shows that $\bar e$ is open. The open-unit groupoid lemma, applied to the flat locally finitely presented projections proved in step 4, now gives that $\bar s,\bar t$ are etale.

source.place: Tag 06N0, cartesian unit square and final paragraph (04R9, 02G5, 02GV).

proof.text: The fppf groupoid presentation lemma makes $b:\bar U\to[\bar U/\bar R]\simeq\mathcal Z$ representable, surjective, flat and locally finitely presented, with self-relation $\bar R$. After base change along this cover $b$, the morphism $b$ is one of $\bar s,\bar t$, which are etale by step 5. Target-local descent of etaleness therefore proves that $b$ is etale. By step 3 its source is the spectrum of the field $k_0$, giving the required morphism $z$. The construction used local Noetherianity only to obtain the initial finitely presented field cover; it required no perfectness of either field and no Noetherianity of $S$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 06N0 (lemma-DM-residual-gerbe), entire proof, formulated directly over S; correcting R-invariant to P-invariant in the quotient-field sentence.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unramified_diagonal_singleton_field_cover {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hstack : IsModuliStack F) (hdiag : HasAlgebraicSpaceDiagonal F) (U : Over S) (atlas : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) F) (hatlas : IsSmoothModuliAtlas F U atlas) (hreduced : ∀ x : U.left, _root_.IsReduced (U.left.presheaf.stalk x)) (hnoetherian : IsLocallyNoetherian U.left) (hsingleton : ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (s : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S) (x : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj (Over.mk s))) F), ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] (t : Spec (.of L) ⟶ S) (y : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj (Over.mk t))) F), ∃ (E : Type u) (_ : Field E) (e : Spec (.of E) ⟶ S) (i : Over.mk e ⟶ Over.mk s) (j : Over.mk e ⟶ Over.mk t), Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map i)).comp x) ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map j)).comp y))) (hunramified : HasUnramifiedModuliDiagonal F) : ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (s : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj (Over.mk s))) F), ∀ (T : Over S) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) F), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange a T t Z p ∧ SpaceMapIsEtale Z T p ∧ SpaceMapIsSurjective Z T p
